digest.component_or_area: Tickets branch delivery and CAS push orchestration
propositions: Duplicate CAS push and fetch-merge-retry loops were consolidated from workflows into a single Python core module (src/rebar/_store/push.py) that owns delivery mechanics with a five-cycle retry budget and terminal push decision

Strict delivery mode (strict=True) raises PushDeliveryError with stable reason codes and unpushed-commit count; best-effort mode (strict=False, default) preserves backward compatibility for library, CLI, MCP, and importer callers
The locked commit-and-push entrypoint (commit_and_push_tickets_branch) stages, commits, and delivers transactions atomically with established bot identity and subject, used by bridge workflows
Workflow adapters (reconcile-bridge and reconcile-bridge-canary) now delegate delivery exactly once through Python strict entrypoints instead of maintaining their own fetch/merge/retry logic
The private adapter (python -m rebar._store.push) translates typed core failures to process exit codes and stderr, keeping core functions reusable and free of sys.exit calls
Legacy callers across Python library, CLI, MCP server, and automation retain their original best-effort defaults and return/disposition contracts without silent strict mode injection
